data.narrative:
Mytra, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Chris Walti and Ahmad Baitalmal, has raised over $200M to date. The valuation assessment relies on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms at Series B through Series D, including Hadrian, Nimble Robotics, Exotec, and Dexterity, alongside one public comparable.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach uses the $200M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $340M. The peer-median method triangulates across five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B, Series C)—producing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B.

The two-method triangulation yields a low estimate of $289M, median of $995M, and high of $1.9B. Material uncertainties include Mytra's specific revenue scale and unit economics relative to peers, retention of customer concentration, and execution risk in manufacturing scaling. The peer-median approach carries greater weight given Mytra's direct stage and sector alignment with sampled companies; however, the wide dispersion ($1.0B to $2.0B) reflects genuine heterogeneity within early-stage robotics valuations. A valuation range of $900M to $1.3B appears most defensible pending disclosure of operating metrics.
